[Nissaraṇīya+sutta]  CL=7 The discourse in which the Buddha teaches the bhikkhus about the three bases of liberation (nissaraṇa dhatu):
Nekkhamma dhatu, the quality of renunciation associated with the first jhāna, leading to liberation from the domain of sensual pleasures (kāmāvacara dhamma); Arūpa dhatu, the formless absorptions, which lead to liberation from the domain of form (rūpāvacara dhamma); Nirodha dhatu, Nibbāna, which is the ultimate liberation from all conditioned phenomena (saṅkhata dhamma) that arise dependent on causes and conditions. A bhikkhu who fully understands these dhammas achieves liberation from kāma (sensual pleasures), rūpa (material forms), and saṅkhata (conditioned phenomena) through samuccheda vimutti—the complete cutting off of defilements. Such a bhikkhu, having fulfilled the tasks of higher knowledge (abhiññā), is peaceful and tranquil, and has transcended the four yokes (bondages).

The Abhidhāna (1073), Amarakosa (19, 83), and its commentary Mahesvara indicate that number words from "dvi" to "aṭṭhārasa" only express countable objects, not numerical values. [Udāna.Ṭ.385. Nīti.pada.p.100 also refer]. Examples: 5 items, 5 kinds, 5 types, 5 persons (etc.).
